data.description:
## Observation (2026-08-13, fleet bug bash)
Every rebar write (comment/edit/close) auto-pushes the tickets branch, and each push triggers its own Reconcile Bridge CI run. A fleet of ~8 concurrent implementers generates a near-continuous stream of runs (observed ~every 3 min), competing with code-change Verified gates for GitHub Actions runners — 1704's pytest matrix queued ~2 hours behind this traffic during the bug bash.

## Idea
Debounce/coalesce tickets-branch CI triggers: e.g. concurrency-group the Reconcile Bridge workflow per branch with cancel-in-progress (newest push wins), or a short trigger cooldown, so N rapid ticket-event pushes cost ~1 run instead of N. Verified gates on code changes keep priority.

## Constraints
- Reconciler correctness must not depend on per-push runs (it reconciles state, so newest-wins coalescing should be safe — verify).
- Do not reduce the *responsiveness* of bridge reconciliation beyond a bounded delay.
- Evidence and sizing before implementation: count tickets-push runs vs code runs over the bug-bash window from the Actions API.
data.title: Debounce CI triggers on tickets-branch pushes (runner contention)
